## Why

An option card shows only the newest set of options for a stop or a stay's lodging. Once the user asks for more options, or for a higher or lower tier, the earlier set is gone from the page. And once the user picks an option, the card closes for good. To look at the options again, the user has to ask the agent.

In Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30 (agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`), he was on the fence between Twelve and Fore Street for the Portland dinner. He picked Twelve in turn 9. To compare the two again later, he would have had to ask the agent, since there was no way to bring the card back. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-30.

The data is already there, so this is a change to the API's view and the page, not to the trip:

- Every candidate is saved with a set number, and asking for more options adds a new set without removing the old ones (domain model 3.9).
- Selecting an option removes no candidates. Only turning one down does.
- The newest-set filter is in `optionCardOf()` in `src/api/itinerary-view.ts`. A stop or stay with a selection gets `card: null`.

The agent needs no change. Selecting from an older set, or from a reopened card, sends the same message as today, such as "Select Twelve for dinner in Portland." The agent already handles switching a pick by name in chat (functional spec 7.5).

A turned-down place is removed, so it won't show when looking back. That's fine, since the user said no to it.

## Design

- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 7.5 (option cards). Its rules change: the card no longer closes for good once an option is selected, and the user can step back through earlier sets.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 3.9 (candidates and set numbers).

## Open questions

- ~~What does the card show for a stop or stay with a selection? Proposal: no card by default, as today, plus a "See options" button that opens it. The open card marks the pick, and its newest set shows first.~~ Settled 2026-10-30, in chat:
  - The card still closes when the user picks, as today. A stop or stay with a pick shows the pick, plus a "See options" button.
  - The button opens the card in place, with the newest set first and the pick marked in it. Another button closes it again.
  - Selecting another option from a reopened card sends the same message as any card's Select, such as "Select Fore Street for dinner in Portland." The agent handles the switch, as it does when the user asks in chat.
  - The button shows only when the stop or stay has a candidate other than the pick. One whose only candidate is the pick, such as a place the user named, gets none.
  - As with every card, it shows only in a session's itinerary view, not on the trip page.
- ~~How does the user move between sets? Proposal: back and forward arrows on the card, with "Set 2 of 3" or similar. The newest set shows first.~~ Settled 2026-10-30, in chat:
  - Back and forward arrows on the card, with "Set 2 of 3" between them. The newest set shows first. The arrows show only when there's more than one set.
  - The count goes by position, not by the saved set number. A set whose candidates were all turned down is gone, so set numbers can skip.
  - "More options", "Higher tier", and "Lower tier" show only on the newest set. An older set shows only Select on each option. Their messages say "these", such as "Show me something nicer than these for dinner in Portland", and the agent reads "these" as the newest set.
  - When a new set arrives, the card goes back to the newest set.
- Do "More options", "Higher tier", and "Lower tier" stay on a reopened card for a selected item? Today, new options for a selected item get no card, and the agent names them in chat (functional spec 7.5). Proposal: keep the actions, and drop that rule, so the new set shows on the reopened card like any other.
- Should this come before "Redo the web UI with Claude Design" (#204)? Proposal: yes. That issue changes only how the app looks, and this changes what the page does. Built first, the redo then designs the arrows and the button along with the rest.

## Do

To be written once the open questions are settled. Already known:

- Update functional spec 7.5 to match, in the same PR.

## Done when

To be written once the open questions are settled.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
